tutorial.title: Response Handling
tutorial.descriptionContent: Work with the response object to unpack the data you need

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Making the API call is only the first part; you also need to properly handle the response, check the status, and extract the data you need.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
When making an API call, we get back a response object that contains the status code, headers, and the actual content we receive.

If we print the response object, we see the status code.

Make sure to pick response, followed by response.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When you make an API call, you get a response object containing the status code, headers, and returned content.

Store the GET response in response, then print that object to inspect its status.

Make sure to pick response, followed by requests.get, and finally response.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Every response object includes a status code indicating the result of the request.

We access the status code using response.status_code.

Make sure to pick response, followed by ., and finally status_code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Every response object includes a status code indicating the result of the request.

You access the status code with response.status_code. Print that numeric code.

Make sure to pick print, followed by response, and finally status_code.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
A 2xx status code indicates a successful request.

Specific codes like 200 OK mean the request was processed correctly, while 201 Created indicates a new resource was successfully created.

Make sure to pick response, followed by ., and finally status_code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A 2xx status code indicates a successful request.

A 200 OK means the request was processed, while 201 Created means a new resource was created.

Store this response's status in status, then print it so the console shows 200.

Make sure to pick status, followed by response.status_code, and finally status.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
A 4xx status code indicates a client error, meaning the request was invalid or cannot be fulfilled.

Examples include 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, and 404 Not Found.

Make sure to pick response, followed by ., and finally status_code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A 4xx status code indicates a client error, meaning the request was invalid or cannot be fulfilled.

Examples include 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, and 404 Not Found.

Request the missing Pokémon mimo, then print the response property that shows 404.

Make sure to pick "https://pokedex.mimo.dev/api/pokemon/mimo", followed by response, and finally status_code.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Print the status code of the response object.

Make sure to pick response, followed by ., and finally status_code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Store the response's status code in code, then print code.

Make sure to pick code, followed by response.status_code, and finally code.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What will this code print, assuming there is no Pokémon called Mimo.

404200

Make sure to pick 404.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You change mimo to pikachu in the URL, and the API successfully returns that existing Pokémon.

Which status now matches the result?

200 OK, because the request succeeded201 Created, because you created a Pokémon404 Not Found, because the URL changed

200 OK, because the request succeeded.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy - - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Access the status code of the response object.

Make sure to pick response, followed by ., and finally status_code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Print the response's status code as the message Status: 200.

Make sure to pick f, followed by response, and finally status_code.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
How would you retrieve the status code of a response from an HTTP request?

By using response.status_codeBy using response.code

By using response.status_code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A response object exposes its status through status_code.

Your response is stored in result. Which expression retrieves its status?

result.status_coderesult.codestatus_code(result)

Make sure to pick result.status_code.

lessons.title: Lesson #9 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does a status code of 404 signify in a response?

It means the requested resource was not foundIt indicates the request was not authorized

It means the requested resource was not found.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your requests return 401 and 404.

Which response tells you to check the requested resource path rather than your authentication details?

The 404 responseThe 401 responseBoth responses mean the resource was not found

Make sure to pick The 404 response.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's explore how to work with JSON data in API responses, a common format for exchanging information between clients and servers.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
We’ve already seen the response object; we need the very same one to parse and work with JSON data returned from the API.

Make sure to pick response, followed by response.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need the same response object to inspect the request and later parse the JSON data returned by the API.

Store the GET result in api_response, then print that object.

Make sure to pick api_response, followed by requests.get, and finally api_response.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can unwrap the JSON data from this response using the json function.

Make sure to pick .json().
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can unwrap the JSON data from this response using the json function.

Parse the response into data, then print the parsed value.

Make sure to pick data, followed by .json(), and finally data.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
When working with an API, it often helps to print the full response data to see if we receive what we expect.

Make sure to pick data, followed by response.json(), and finally data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can print the full response data to check whether you receive what you expect.

Parse the document into pokemon, then print the full parsed data.

Make sure to pick pokemon, followed by pokemon, and finally response.json().

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
In Python, JSON data is parsed into a dictionary-like structure, allowing you to access values using keys.

We define the key as a string inside square brackets to access the corresponding value in the dictionary.

Make sure to pick [, followed by "name", and finally ].
lessons.hardModeContent:
In Python, JSON data is parsed into a dictionary-like structure, allowing you to access values using keys.

You define each key as a string inside square brackets.

Print the Pokémon's name, then its ID, on separate lines.

Make sure to pick data, followed by "name", data, and finally "id".

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
As long as the dictionary has the key we're using, we can access as many fields as we want.

Make sure to pick data, followed by data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
As long as the dictionary has the key we're using, we can access as many fields as we want.

Use data to print pikachu, then 4, from the matching fields.

Make sure to pick data, followed by "name", data, and finally "height".

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
When working with JSON data, sometimes the top level is an array, meaning the entire response is a list of objects rather than a single one.

Make sure to pick data, followed by data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You may receive a JSON array at the top level: a list of objects instead of one object.

Parse this array into data, then print the entire list of Pokémon objects.

Make sure to pick data, followed by response.json(), and finally data.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Once you've unpacked the array, you can loop through its elements or directly access an item by its index.

Make sure to pick for followed by pokemon and then in, data.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Once you've unpacked the array, you can loop through its elements or directly access an item by its index.

Loop through every Pokémon and print its name and ID in the shown format.

Make sure to pick pokemon, followed by for, data, pokemon['name'], and finally pokemon['id'].

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
You can directly access elements using their index if you're working with an array as the top-level structure.

Make sure to pick data followed by [ and then 0, ].
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can directly access elements using their index if you're working with an array as the top-level structure.

Store the first object in first, then print its name so the console shows bulbasaur.

Make sure to pick first, followed by data, 0, first, and finally "name".

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Unwrap the JSON data from this response using the json function.

Make sure to pick response followed by . and then json, ().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Unwrap the JSON data from this response using the json function.

Print the parsed JSON directly without storing it in another variable.

Make sure to pick print, followed by response, ., json, and finally ().

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Assuming the response is an array, access the first value.

Make sure to pick data followed by [ and then 0, ].
lessons.hardModeContent:
The response is a top-level array. Print its second Pokémon object, which represents ivysaur.

Make sure to pick data, followed by [, 1, and finally ].

lessons.title: Lesson #5 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use bracket notation to access data in a JSON object.

Make sure to pick data followed by [ and then "name", ].
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use bracket notation on the parsed JSON object to print the Pokémon ID 25.

Make sure to pick data, followed by [, "id", and finally ].
